China Clothing Manufacturer & Uniform Supplier | LF Clothing
Meet LF Clothing, a custom clothing manufacturer with our own factory in China. We develop, sample and produce uniforms, workwear and branded apparel.
Can we start with a reference image and no technical specification?

Yes. Send a photo, sketch or AI concept and tell us who will wear the clothing and how it will be used. We help work out the fabric, fit and construction, then develop a sample you can check. You do not need a finished tech pack to begin.
Can suits, polos, workwear and caps share the same brand identity?

Yes. Your reception, service and operations teams can wear different garments while sharing one brand identity. We use your colour references and artwork across the range, choosing suitable embroidery, printing or labels for each fabric. Samples let you check the items together before production.
How do semi-custom and fully custom orders differ in cost, minimums and timing?

If an existing garment already suits your team, start with logo, label or selected detail changes. Choose full development when you need a different fabric, fit, pocket layout or construction. Price depends on the development work, garment quantity and materials. Minimums and timing depend on the chosen style and changes.
Can you provide fabric reports or arrange finished-garment testing?

We can provide relevant fabric reports and arrange finished-garment testing. Include any required standard or performance requirement in your brief so the quote can account for it. Testing of custom finished garments carries an additional fee. Fabric reports cover the material; they do not certify the finished garment.
When does sampling start, and can you work to our event date?

Clothing samples take 7–12 days after order confirmation and sample payment. Tell us the date the garments need to arrive and the delivery destination, rather than only the event date. We plan backwards through shipping, production and sample approval. Production time depends on the products, materials, quantities and customisation.
Can we order one product category or a coordinated range?

Both are welcome. Send one list covering the clothing, caps, footwear, towels or PPE your team needs, with quantities for each item. LF brings the requirements together and coordinates the relevant suppliers, so your purchasing team has one point of contact. Options, minimums and schedules can vary by item.
Do you manufacture clothing in your own factory?

We manufacture garments in our own factory. LF handles specifications, materials, patterns, samples, production, quality checks and packing. Your team works directly with us from the initial brief to shipment.
How are PPE and construction safety helmets reviewed?

Tell us the product, intended use, destination and required standard. We check the supporting documents and whether the proposed colour, logo or other changes are suitable. PPE and helmet requirements are assessed for each product; clothing or fabric certificates do not automatically cover them.

Corporate Uniforms Questions
Should we update existing uniforms or develop new garments?

If the current style works well, start with branding, colours or selected detail changes. Full development suits a brief that calls for a different fabric, fit or construction. Both routes follow your quality requirements. We explain the materials, quantities and development costs in your quotation.
What is the minimum order for regular staff clothing?

The usual minimum is 50 garments per style/colour for regular clothing orders. Send the quantities needed for each item and staff group so we can plan the range and prepare the quotation. Footwear, towels, PPE and other related products have their own ordering requirements, which we discuss for the items you select.
Can we start with pictures instead of a technical pack?

Yes. Reference photos, an AI concept, a sketch or an existing garment are enough to begin. Show what you like and what needs to change. We help develop the practical specification for sampling, including fabric, measurements, garment details and branding.
When does sampling start, and how long does an order take?

After order confirmation and payment of the sample fee, we start sampling as soon as possible. Clothing samples take 7–12 days. Bulk timing depends on each product, quantity and customisation, including approvals and material readiness. We set out the item schedules and shipping separately against your required arrival dates. For orders of 200 pieces or more of the same style, the sample fee can be credited against the bulk order payment.
Can our purchasing team request test reports?

Yes. We can arrange fabric and finished-garment testing and provide reports for your purchasing team. Tests on custom finished garments carry an additional fee, with scope and cost set out beforehand. Tell us the tests or standards you need; PPE and other protective items require evidence for the particular product and intended use.
How do you help keep repeat staff orders consistent?

We retain one garment from each bulk order to help align future orders with the original production. It provides a reference for fit, construction and branding when you need clothing for additional staff or departments. Material and trim availability is checked again before a repeat order is arranged.
How are samples shipped, and is shipping included?
Sample shipping is charged separately. Samples are usually sent by express courier on DDP terms.
How long does bulk production take, and what deposit is required?
For regular bulk orders of up to 500 pieces, production usually takes 2–3 weeks from receipt of the 30% deposit. Shipping time is additional.
When is the balance due, and can we inspect the order?
We require a 30% deposit, with the remaining 70% balance paid in full before shipment. Video inspection and in-person inspection are available before dispatch.
How do you check and pack the order before dispatch?

We record quality inspection and packing videos before shipment. Garments with obvious quality or appearance issues identified during inspection are remade before packing and are not dispatched with those issues.
How are defects in a delivered bulk order handled?

If defects are found after delivery, we review the issues against the approved sample and specifications. Compensation is agreed case by case, taking the defect rate and other relevant factors into account.
